Title: Control Ultimate Edition

Verdict - pick up on deep sale.

Overall - 6.6/10

Control has a very interesting story and great audio, but all other aspects of the game being just OK, gameplay being bland at best.
I would prefer to consume this story in another medium like book or show, to be honest.


Graphics: 6/10

The brutalism of the old house space is cool, albeit grey and bland. Nothing exceptional, character models just OK. but gets the job done.

Audio: 7/10

The unsettling chanting of the hiss, the ambiance, gunshots, and tense music during set pieces was GREAT.

Performance: 8/10

Played on PS Portal. Only hiccups were due to streaming issues. Runs with no issues.

Gameplay: 5/10

Using the map to navigate took awhile to get used to, but was never really excellent. Read that the goal was to get people to read signs instead of map. BLEH

Movement - levitation, dashing, slamming - pretty fun.

AWEs, OoP, weird paranormal stuff. I read everything I picked up, watched every Dr Langston Video, and listened to every audio recording. This is the part that makes me interested into going further into the Remedy Universe.

Looks very nice but that's about it.

I was initially hyped for this game. I liked the first half of Quantum Break but it got long in the tooth. Finally I get my hands on it and now I see why it hasn't garnered much enthusiasm. It feels like several overachievers saved this game from total annihilation. Art direction and style are great. Whatever they're doing to make the visuals pop is technical wizardry. Lighting, physics, particle effects, and color theory make this game memorable. The combat is fun yet highly repetitive. Throwing things is really cool for the first two minutes. There isn't much creativity when it comes to the combat.

Onto the bad... The extremely convoluted story isn't helped by the extremely bland characters. At first the scenario is intriguing but it gets repetitive so quickly. I could feel myself constantly eye rolling. The level design is terrible. It's not fun running through these completely random hallways that have no logic to them. Stairways and blocked corridors just seem to pop out of nowhere. And it's not like the "ooh isn't surreal?" type of random, it's the "hurry we need this to be done in three hours" kind of random. The collectibles are stale and littered everywhere. The enemies are so boring. Most of them are soldiers that simply run and gun. They barely throw grenades at you.

I will be giving this game a couple more hours as I hear it picks up when you unlock more powers. But man it's really boring so far.

Control: Ultimate Edition — Never Again❌

I forced myself to finish Control Ultimate Edition purely out of willpower, and every side quest felt like a chore. I admire anyone who finished the game multiple times—they have my respect. Honestly, I don't understand the hype surrounding this game at all. Finishing it was complete agony—especially considering the base game takes only about 11 hours to complete, yet they still dare to charge 40€ for it. That price tag for this experience is absolutely ridiculous.

➕Pros:
Upgrades & Gear: The weapon modification system, player upgrades, and clean UI are well-designed and easy to navigate.

Alan Wake Tie-in: The crossover elements with the Alan Wake universe were a pleasant touch.

Cutscenes: Visual quality of the cutscenes is high (though content-wise, they consist mostly of plain dialogue with little engagement).

➖Cons:
Horrible Map & Navigation: The map is absolute garbage. Instead of enjoying the story, you spend most of your time lost, trying to figure out how to even get to your objective.

Relentless Respawn: Enemies respawn almost instantly. Walk through a door, step into a hallway for two seconds, and when you turn back, a full squad of enemies has already spawned. It’s a constant, exhausting struggle for survival in a place where you're already lost.

Clunky Controls & Telekinesis: Shooting feels punchy, though aiming is noticeably inaccurate. However, the launch/levitation mechanic is horribly annoying—Jesse constantly picks up objects you didn't intend to target, which ruins boss fights.

Absurd & Unfair Difficulty: Boss fights feel like cheap Souls-like encounters without any option to adjust the difficulty. They are frustrating and buggy. Even with fully upgraded stats and top-tier mods, bosses can two-shot you. It quickly becomes demotivating, tedious, and completely ruins the experience.

Final Score: 3/10
Excellent game. A lot of reading but great story. I do get lost a lot, even with the map, because of multiple levels. Runs flawlessly on M3 Pro Mac.

I bought a RTX card only to play this game full quality, because I loved Alan Wake and the images of the game showed cool brutalist architecture and a misterious mood that haunted me. So, I was really enthusiastic with the game and ready to forgive anything, as I did in Alan Wake with the controls and the ending. Ok, couldn't. Some feelings:
- The map is terrible, confusing and wothless sometimes.
- The gameplay. I was ok with the idea of a third person shooter until I arrived to the first hiss. A lot of people, cover didn't work, running didn't work, pointing with the controller was near impossible. I died like 50 times and looked at the menu for an auto-aim or something, there was a giant cheat menu that boosted up your gun. Cool because it helped me to keep going on, and sad because it shows how badly balanced the game is. Even with all the stats up, the shooting never felt funny or engaging. The fx and illumination didn't help to find the enemies too.
- The cutscenes were pure cringe. Strange pacing, hearing the main character thoughs was annoying and the writing and characters weren't great.
- Choosing the third person camera perspective totally kills the mood of the game. In a FPS the environment could be more oppresive and moody, but in this perspective the camera covers very long open areas, so you're running through very repetitive halls (using the same assets because they need to fill all the empty space) and watching things come from a mile away.
- The story isn't great, and having a 1000 documents scattered around just makes you lo…

citations.review_text: It's a fine, well made game. Though, I have no attachment to the story and the gun play gets repetitive.

I decided to finish this game before Resonant comes out to catch up on the story and lore and everything, and it kinda was a very ordinary playthrough. Yeah, graphics are nice, and yeah, combat is fun, albeit a bit repetitive at times, and yeah, style and architecture stand out.... 

And then I reached Mission 9. 
Holy **** 
 
If nothing else, Control is worth playing for Mission 9 alone

8 out of 10

I really enjoyed playing through this game. The style and location design are really cool. The live-action video segments with real people are integrated unusually well. Overall, it’s a pretty atmospheric adventure, and that’s what gets a thumbs up from me.

As for the downsides, I’d point out the rather repetitive combat: you either throw objects or shoot one of a couple of guns. That’s it. And while throwing stuff does look satisfying, by the second half of the game it does start to wear thin.

The story is not for everyone: I’m personally not a big fan of paranormal stuff, but I have to admit that overall it’s pretty well written.

Story, lore bits, cinematic feeling of the game is 9/10, everything else is either mid or really bad. 

Starting with combat, emptying your mags in first hour of the game is fun but then it becomes sad as just throwing objects on cooldown simplifies the combat and makes it unfun for rest of the game.

Enemies constantly respawn in places you cleared just slowing you down in progress of the game, bosses that you fight are extremely weak, after you kill them they start spawning in normal groups of enemies and those versions are stronger than the bosses by a lot. 

A bit of spoilers here [spoiler] skills you obtain throughout the game don't really do much apart from getting to places quicker dashes/levitation (levitation is absolutely horrible to control), the blocking skill is basically not needed. [/spoiler]

Skill tree upgrades are very boring, mods for your gun and body are just chore that fills up your inventory having to manage it, the game would be thousand times better without that system because you just put on the highest rarity of stuff you want and don't do anything else with it. Crafting of new guns should have just been unlocking new guns from quests, materials just drop and there is nothing really about them that would make you like great i got that. New guns are also not needed and i found them quite boring.

Characters in game talk a lot to themselves and in between each other, eavesdropping on them can be fun sometimes. Story a bit blows at the end but it might also be because i didn't do many sidequests before that and the game kind of just ended at some point. 

Can't recommend the game based on combat and the rpg elements yanked in without which the game would be so much better and maybe longer in story.

A well made game with beautiful graphics, great in slowly building the story you just fall into, but, yeah, the combat doesn't really evolve and feels repetitive and kinda boring. So, a warning, not to let me spoil your fun, but in the end it seems more about combat than story. That could be just what you want.
In Tomb Raider there is also exploration and puzzling, but here there is more combat. The enemy is also not very engaging. Rather anonymous entities that get in the way of running around in an otherwise very empty office building. I admit I did quit early after 4 hours, but that was the point where they started throwing grenades at me...dodging explosives is not my thing. 
I cannot not recommend this. It's been a hell of a job creating this, but it's not for everyone.

Impeccable world design. Gameplay is bleak, dull and tiresome. This is the first game that I decided to play regardless of my averseness to an horror & thriller genre. I stayed because of the story, the mystery. The art design is top of the notch. The visuals, the world design, character development, the writing of the collectibles, niche puzzles, actors in the videos: they are all engaging. Attention to detail is very thought-out. Some areas such as the ashtray maze are astonishing. It turns out that there was one more sector, which was considered to be a DLC, yet I refused to face the same types of enemies and combat over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over again; so I decided to just uninstall it after completing the main story-line and accidentally one DLC. I will give my experience 7 out of 10.

Havent finished it yet but its a very fun game.

Gameplay- 7.5/10 (pretty repetitive but it has fresh ideas and its challenges you to use logic)
Game design- 8.5/10 (again feels really fresh and original)
Story- 7.5 (pretty interesting but lacks longivity)

Overall - 8.5/10 

Grab it on sale, its a fresh and fun game.

As much as I wanted to like this game having played and liked all of Remedy's previous games and really enjoyed Quantum Break, I just could not get into it. The levels are rather bland, ugly and uninteresting, gameplay is also rather repetitive and not that fun. Story is a bit better, but unfolds quite slowly. There's plenty of backtracking and fighting the same fights over and over. Can't really recommend this game and I can't see myself finishing it - I've played as much as I possibly could, but I won't waste another minute on it. Only relieve for me is that I bought it on sale for the price of a cup of coffee pretty much, but I can't imagine paying full price for it.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that textures fail to load properly, appearing blurry or low-resolution.

citations.review_text:
The game is good. 

One issue I encountered was the textures not loading to full res. Causing some instances where I couldn't read context clues in the environment. The only way I managed to fix this was by opening up the options menu and closing it again, everytime I needed to look at textures. Fixable with a mod, or so I've heard. 

Good game otherwise.

I was so psyched for this game, I heard all the good reviews and really wanted to play but I'm having endless graphical issues with this game. The texture loading issue is still there which makes half the assets in the game look like a blurry mess of pixels. I'm also having an issue with the lighting in the game - weird sparkles all over the place. Lastly, after about 20 minutes of playing, the game will just start stuttering like crazy. I tried all the different graphics settings from low to medium, disable raytracing, decrease render resolution, etc but nothing helps. This game is a mess and I wish I could get my money back.

Graphics are glorious. Definitely a different style of third person game. Super fun powers to use, and the story is quite mysterious. If you love paranormal stuff and sci-fi this is definitely for you.

Some bugs with textures, but easily fixed with a couple of easy to install mods from nexus.

An incredible exploration of an SCP-like office. Seen other reviews say the story is hard to follow, and that the combat is boring.

I'm not sure how they think that. The story is compelling, and at times hilarious (if you bother to peruse all the stuff you pick up. Sorry, you gotta read. You can read. It's worth it.) I'm, I think 2/3 through the game and I greatly enjoy telekinetically flinging sofas, lamps, and other sundries at my foes while levitating. It's incredibly satisfying. If you're bored, just max your psychic throw. You can thank me later.

Do the side quests. Explore. It's worth it, because the things you'll find definitely will make combat not be "boring" (what are those guys even talking about?)

My only complaint is the weird issue of textures going completely low res when they have no reason to on my rig. Even with the mod to force more aggressive texture loading, I still have some issues. It sounds like something that has been going on consistently for a while, and it's a real shame in a game this gorgeous.

The game is an absolute blast to play, and it looks stunning with its vibrant red ambience enhanced by ray tracing. I strongly recommend playing with ray tracing enabled—not just here, but also in other Remedy titles like Alan Wake 2.

That said, there’s one notable issue: textures often fail to load properly, even when set to Ultra. The fix is straightforward: set DLSS to Quality, max out your graphics settings, then close the game. After that, head to the installation folder and launch the game using Control_DX11.exe. Once you do this, the texture problem disappears.

claims.claim: Reviewers point out that the game suffers from stutters and performance issues requiring manual tweaks or launch options to fix.

citations.review_text:
Control is a very immersive experience indeed. The story and gunplay were great, the mods made weapons significantly stronger, and the launch ability was very fun - especially when you upgrade it to the maximum. The Foundation DLC was cool, giving a more satisfying end. The game is pretty optimized (I had to switch to DX11), and the experience was very smooth.

Overall a great experience, must buy 9/10!

I was so psyched for this game, I heard all the good reviews and really wanted to play but I'm having endless graphical issues with this game. The texture loading issue is still there which makes half the assets in the game look like a blurry mess of pixels. I'm also having an issue with the lighting in the game - weird sparkles all over the place. Lastly, after about 20 minutes of playing, the game will just start stuttering like crazy. I tried all the different graphics settings from low to medium, disable raytracing, decrease render resolution, etc but nothing helps. This game is a mess and I wish I could get my money back.

Control is a fun game with amazing graphics and a fun combat system (Reminds me of Infamous with its flow). 

There is alot of lore in this game with all the collectables around the world which you can read and find tons of information. 

Two issues I've had that ruined it for me. The map can be quite confusing at some points with no clear direction. Sometimes finding the right floor/level to be on can be confusing to the point I'm just running around trying to find the objective. The second issue which was the biggest is the performance; specifically the stutters. Theres a few guides online with changing power modes to high performance etc but I think it's silly to have to do that at all. Especially on a 9950X3D which needs Balanced mode for the parking to work correctly. The stuttering ruined the enjoyment the most for me. 

Controls world/enviroment is eerie, fluid/satisfying combat and has an interesting story. If these interest you, then I'd recommend Control.

Combat in this game is flashy, but not enjoyable. The guns are peashooters and you are reduced to just spamming launch the whole game and even then half of the enemies you will encounter just instantly dodge the ability. I find it hard to believe that the same studio that made Max Payne made this game.

The game is themeatically fun. If you like any combination of the following you'll probably like the story and the world: Creepypastas, The X-Files, The Backrooms, SCP Foundation, The Matrix, David Lynch movies, Inception, Half-Life, Portal, and S.T.A.L.K.E.R. With that being said, the game is pretty derivative. You can tell it's a patchwork rather than an intricate weave of elements. 

The story is...nonsensical. You are expected to read and watch a ♥♥♥♥ load of collectables to fully grasp it. Somehow even though the story is nonsensical, the ending or "twist" was pretty damn obvious. You will probably spend more time reading/watching the collectibles than you will actually playing the game.

The game is also quite buggy and unoptimised. I recommend playing with -dx11 in the launch options. Do not alt-tab at any point during the credits or you will not get achievements for the related mission(s).

Conclusion: If the gameplay of the video game, was better, I would recommend this game. I bought this on sale. I probably would never recommend this for full price. Unfortunate.

citations.review_text:
Control rests on the it's excellent level design, atmosphere, cryptic lore, and sound design, and makes it a game that is almost a masterpiece.

But let me first describe things that belew my mind was the architecture of the Old House, wow, the way they have used brutalist architecture with the supernatural and surreal is incredible.

Secondly, the sound design is shockingly good, and so is the sense of discovery due to the level design with lore around each corner which gives you short snippets into the unfolding cryptic tale Remedy has threaded across its games.

Thirdly, the side missions, most of them are just worth doing as they are great, and well scripted, some are a little filler, but generally definitely worth it, and the perks of upgrading your character is a huge bonus for the later combat scenarios.

Lastly, the voice acting is also pretty much at point, along with performances, a highlight for sure, so is the DLCs, definitely one of the more excellent DLC expansions to a game with rich lore.

But there are a few small design issues that hold the game from becoming a 10/10:

One is the repeating enemy types, with just higher difficulty levels. The variety is a little low, but the world, and its metroidvania style of structure eases this a bit, but Remedy probably needs to improve on this for their upcoming sequel.

Two, is the map in the game. It is confusing, and tedious to use. I get that Remedy probably wanted you to be lost in the Old House like it was meant to be, and explore each corner to find your way through sign posting, but after sometime it becomes a little tedious, and also the sign-posting is not perfect, so can be frustrating.

Finally, certain combats are in red lighting  and also the enemies glow with red, and red affect, so when there is a lot of stuff on the screen can be difficult to see. I think there should been a variation in the colour palette to make the enemies stand out a little more. 

These are the 3 things I found irriating …

It was ultimately pretty solid. The combat gets routine and, while the lore pages are interesting and add a lot, they really break up game momentum. If you aren't into story telling by in game lore, this is definitely not for you. The map is also pretty hard to get used to. Lighting isn't great at times. Though, for the amount of times this goes on sale I'd definitely say it is worth it. I played The Foundation but was honestly a bit too burnt out to do the AWE expansion.

Missions that leave you completely lost, a terrible map, repetitive combat, boring enemies, and exploration that feels like a complete waste of time. A game designed to frustrate you instead of letting you have fun. Rating: 0/10.

I wanted to like this game - it's got an intriguing plot, a really nice artistic and production style and direction, and generally decent overall design, but the map system and boss battles (generally combat in late-game and DLC) are trash which totally killed the mood and patience I had for the entire experience - fake difficulty by adding random holes on the ground or bad camera systems locking you into corners, which make combat frustrating for a heroine who is totally OP.  You don't feel OP, nor did I ever feel intrigued by the story and vague clues.  Felt like a chore, but like I said, at least it has good production value.  I don't see any need for replaying it unless you are obsessed with the fiction, and I'll admit I wanted to get into the fiction, but after a short while, I lost all interest and it became a chore since I kept getting lost all the damn time.  It's quite frustrating to have to load a game, die within seconds, only to take even longer to load the same level to rinse and repeat.  Oh and don't bother with the annoying side missions that interrupt your gameplay - the rewards are hardly worth it.  Honestly, it felt like none of it was worth it, even the ending :(  Exploration (with a horrible map) was barely tolerable, and my biggest complaint is that combat feels artificially balanced even though your character is OP.  I won't rate this horribly, but I will give it a 'meh'.  Remedy has done amazing work before, but this one simply didn't click for me, even tying itself with the Alan Wake serires.  I look forward to the next major IP, but I'm glad I'm done with this one.

[i]Control[/i] has a lot of great points, but they don't really "click" together, resulting in a "just ok" game.
That said, there's plenty to enjoy individually :
[list]
[*]It's incredibly beautiful. The architecture of the Bureau is so pleasing, with geometric shapes enhanced by how the light falls on them, and the use of colour is sparse and dramatic. Amazing. If you like brutalism it's a treat, and if you don't, it may change your mind :)
[*]The artistic direction in general is very coherent, so even menuing and getting missions is visually pleasing.
[*]The atmosphere is incredible. You feel the tension, the weirdness, the wrongness. A situation might be ridiculous, but you're so invested that you feel the danger.
[*]The writing and acting are great. You completely believe the research reports, you immediately "get" the characters. It's awesome.
[/list]
Things to be wary of :
[list]
[*]The maps are next to useless. I used them more as compass than anything else. That's a pretty big drawback for a metroivania.
[*]Combat is fairly repetitive. You get a cool gun and cool abilities, but combat is basically use gun, use abilities, run, and repeat. Enemies aren't very varied either.
[*]Combat is [i]hard[/i]. Like, way harder than I expected. I'm definitely not a very skilled player, but I was taking so much damage without even seeing where from, I had no time to learn +_+ (But there are a [i]lot[/i] of assistance options available if needed.)
[*]While I enjoyed reading/listening to the collectibles, there are too. many. of them. You're always interrupting exploration to check them. Same with mods after a while : you're always interrupted because you need to tidy up your inventory.
[/list]
All in all I really liked the game for its beautiful environments and immersive atmosphere, and I do recommend it, but... temper your expectations, maybe ?

control's worldbuilding and lore are compelling as hell, but unfortunately the actual game is not as phenomenally executed. the maps are the worst offenders, not really offering any sort of elevation indicator, dead end indicator, they just get mushed together and stacked on top of each other. this might just be on my system, but my fps was considerably lower when i used a mouse as opposed to a controller, and this game is much less controller-friendly (but still more than manageable). all that being said, it's worth getting to the end of the base game as well as the dlcs to experience how the narrative unfolds, and i am still very excited for a sequel to potentially improve upon the flaws present in this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features destructible environments with advanced physics allowing players to manipulate and throw objects using telekinesis.

citations.review_text:
The game that made me fall in love with Brutalist architecture and introduced me to the wonderous Remedyverse.

Control represented a bit of a milestone for my gaming journey. I first played the game in 2019, back when it was only available on the Epic Games Store. It was also the same year I built my first Desktop PC, which housed my first "real" GPU, the Nvidia RTX 2080Ti. This game came bundled with that graphics card for free as a part of a sale deal I took back then. Once my then new PC was up and running, I wanted to try out a Ray Tracing title to put the rig to the test. Control was the first and perfect candidate. 

Boy, was this game a lot more amazing than I thought it would be. I loved it so much, I decided to purchase it again when it finally arrived on Steam. Then I decided to revisit the game this year to refresh my memory before Control Resonant comes out, and also to get those Steam achievements. 

Even today, I still consider it an amazing game with deliciously good visuals, highly immersive storytelling and directing that feels like you're watching a movie sometimes (which I feel is Remedy's trademark), very cool world-building with huge potential that fans of the SCP Foundation and Men-In-Black type conspiracies (like me!) will absolutely adore, and the most realistic physics i've ever seen in a video game to date. Like seriously, the sheer amount of stuff you can manipulate, throw, or break is just crazy fun. 

My only complaint is that this game is super hard to run at max settings; back in 2019 my PC struggled to get over 60 FPS with Ray Tracing on, and even after upgrading that PC 2 years ago it's still very hard to run today lol. But it's worth it every time just to see the beautiful design of the Oldest House in it's full glory.

Ahti is a CHAD.

I love the physics of the game, it's insanely good even though things fly around here and there.  The game looks very nice which with a 40GB size is unimaginable in today's world of 100GB+ bloated games. The facial expressions when Jesse has a monologue is awesome, it has such a unique feel along with the big texts that pop up when a new area is visited. It all has a certain unique vibe.

The dash making paper and stuff fly around is awesome, I love details like this. The physics of the game are insanely good overall.  

It's weird that Jesse is writing reports on enemies while there's a AWE ongoing in the Oldest House.  I really low how tough the FBC people are. There's unimaginable otherworldly horrors everywhere and they're like "another day on the job". The story is cryptic and has a very good feel about it. 

There were a few bugs like random black squares appearing on the screen, but nothing major. The controls are a bit bad on PC, probably because it's a port. Crafting and inventory management is a bit cluncky. This being a port could be felt a few times thru the game.  The extremely slow gates in the thresholds and the holes in the foundation (where you visibly fit in but the invisible wall stops you) are infuriating tbh.  

My god I've been missing games not having the "fun", "quirky", Marvel-esque oneliners that all new games do. Having a character share their inner monologue in a human, NORMAL manner is so underappreciated. 

Overall, I give it a 8/10. It was pretty good but I probably wont play it again.

[h1]6.8/10[/h1]
                                           [u][h2]Control[/h2][/u]
[b] <Best of TPS/shooty-shooty-bang> [/b] 

+++++ [b]Destructible Environments[/b]: Northlight engine is exquisite. Vast amount of physics objects, destructible foundations, dynamic light sources is staggering. And with the level design focusing on it, this is easily the best part of the game. All with good performance on PC. Couldn't say the same if they've used Unreal.

++++ [b]The Oldest House[/b]: The most important character in the game is the environment itself. The game goes hard on its level design, being inspired by brutalism and surrealism without sacrificing believability. Usually non-eucladian structures like these are used as a excuse to not care about consistency yet in this metroidvania-like game, the map and levels stuck in my head from start to finish. 

+++ [b]Combat and Difficulty[/b]: The game was a power fantasy (it's not hard) without being boring throughout the playthrough. I especially liked the "expeditions", testing the combat's limit. This couldn't happen with a healthy dose of different enemy types. All of the strengths of this game hinges on gameplay and abilities being fun, and it is. 

+ [b]<THE BOARD>[/b]: <It is obligatory/cool as ♥♥♥♥>.

- [b]Too much lore[/b]: Most of the notes you'll find are about the minutiae of Federal Bureau of Control. There are some fun ideas in there but when they find a paranormal activity, they make it a point to at least have 3 different pages about it with the same information. If you like SCP, you'll feel right at home. I just wish they edited down to like -30%.

-- [b]Slow Plot[/b]: The entire plot can be summed as the protaganist coming the terms with being the director. But that's it, i can't tell you what are the turning points in her journey because nothing that happens in the game connects as a larger story. We also had a story about our origin which doesn't go anywhere. 

-- [b]Jesse and most of the cast[/b]: Rela…

Control Ultimate Edition foi mais uma grata surpresa da Remedy.

Depois de terminar Alan Wake 2, eu fiquei completamente maluco pra entender melhor esse universo compartilhado e resolvi finalmente dar uma chance ao Control. E valeu muito a pena.

A maior qualidade da Remedy continua sendo a mesma: narrativa. Os caras criam um universo tão esquisito que você passa o jogo inteiro pensando "que porra tá acontecendo?", mas de um jeito bom. Escritórios burocráticos, objetos amaldiçoados, dimensões paralelas e uma quantidade saudável de maluquice. Não existe outro estúdio fazendo esse tipo de viagem.

A gameplay também é excelente, principalmente pela evolução da Jesse. Você começa relativamente limitado e termina praticamente uma entidade sobrenatural. A telecinese é, de longe, a melhor mecânica do jogo. Você deixa de enxergar o cenário como cenário e passa a enxergá-lo como munição. Mesa, cadeira, concreto, empilhadeira, extintor, inimigos... tudo vira um projétil. A Service Weapon é muito divertida, mas, pra mim, ela acaba sendo quase um complemento. O verdadeiro espetáculo é sair desmontando o ambiente inteiro na base da força bruta.

A progressão acompanha muito bem isso. Você realmente sente que está ficando cada vez mais poderoso, e o jogo sabe introduzir novas habilidades sem deixar tudo repetitivo. No final da campanha você está voando, desviando, explodindo salas inteiras e controlando o campo de batalha de um jeito muito satisfatório.

Visualmente, mesmo sendo um jogo de 2019, ele ainda impressiona bastante. Joguei tudo no máximo, com ray tracing e 120 FPS, então meu hardware obviamente ajudou, mas dá pra ver que a Remedy já fazia um trabalho técnico absurdo naquela época. O único aspecto que envelheceu mal são as expressões faciais. A Jesse parece emocionalmente anestesiada o jogo inteiro. Ela faz praticamente a mesma cara em qualquer situação.

As DLCs têm uma diferença enorme de qualidade. Expeditions eu achei completamente esquecível, parece mai…

[h1]A Beautiful Concept Wrapped in a Boring Game.[/h1]
The atmosphere, the design of the Oldest House, and the visual style are genuinely captivating at first, but unfortunately, the game didn’t live up to my expectations. The story is presented in such a fragmented way that, instead of feeling intrigued, I often found myself confused. The gameplay quickly devolves into repetitive shootouts and clearing rooms, and the built-in invincibility mode made the whole process even more boring. There was simply no reason for me to play on any other difficulty — my main goal was to focus on the story and not waste time dying and repeating the same encounters.

The weapon modification and upgrade systems didn’t interest me either. They felt more like unnecessary busywork that I had absolutely no desire to learn or engage with.

I also want to mention the connection to Alan Wake. Personally, I found it somewhat out of place in this particular game. Alan Wake has its own story and atmosphere, and I much prefer experiencing it as a standalone game rather than seeing it intertwined with Control in this way. Especially considering that there aren’t actually that many Alan Wake-related sections here. There was one moment I genuinely enjoyed, though — the sequence accompanied by music from Poets of the Fall, where you have to navigate a maze-like room with moving walls.

I was ultimately left feeling bored. I frequently found myself thinking, “When is this going to be over?” And after getting all the achievements and reading > 50% of notes, I was completely convinced that this game simply wasn’t for me. Honestly, this is probably [b]the worst game I’ve played in the last 5+ years.[/b]

[h3]A few words about 'Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden'[/h3]
I had a very similar experience with Banishers. In that game, the developers also, in my opinion, force the player to spend far too much time moving around the world and doing unnecessary backtracking. If you focus primarily on the main story q…

One of the best, most atmospheric games I have ever played. The in-game discoverables/collectibles are interesting and worth seeking out. The graphics and sound are top notch. The world building can be cryptic....but if you're playing this kind of game for the X files/mysterious government experiment feel then the lore nails that completely.

The only thing keeping this from being a 10/10 for me is the combat: it started to become repetitive toward the 20-25 hour mark (still fun, just repetitive). Even with the combat, I would rate this game a 9/10.

I have a new PC so I won't attach my specs, but I played this on a GTX1080ti and I had no issues at all with frame rates or having to turn down settings.

Lore and world building is top notch (We'll see a subpar TV adaption of this eventually). Obviously by now you know it's probably heavily SCP inspired, which it is, but it also has it's own unique spin on why things are so weird, and there's plenty of space to keep building further. 

Gameplay is good, it's a bit of a slow build to get the really fun powers, like flying, but that's all part of good game design. I know some people complain the gameplay loop gets a bit repetitive, which it can, but there's a steady enough introduction to new powers and I genuinely found the exploration of the levels fun, so it never felt like it dragged to me. However, if you don't like reading little lore drops, this may not be as fun for you. 

I got the Ultimate edition and really enjoyed the both DLC's. The main issue IMO with this game is the ending for the main story is kind of a let down, there's minimal build up to the third act, and it kinda feels like it just ends without the proper fan fair, which is a shame, because once you get really into a game's world, you'd like a stronger send off. At least gimme a badass last boss. 

If you want a single player story driven game with 30-40 content, then I highly recommend, Control. Overall, 8.8/10

claims.claim: Ray tracing and advanced graphics settings cause performance issues and frame rate drops.

citations.review_text:
Game is in between recommended and not.

A lot of collecting sh!t and reading documents to get some backgound info.
The games visuals are done poorly, some weird RT reflections and/or shadows that does not look good, even with newer hardware than the game release, it still runs bad.
The lighting just pissed me off, like why is it super dark in a room that has multiple stadium flood lights and then some things are super bright in a room/area, but the area itself is still dark af.

But i still recommend the game because it is constantly on sale for 5€ and the story is interesting.
The gameplay is good and because I found the story interesting enough, i will probably check out the newer Control game as well.

Control (and its ultimate edition with the AWE and The Foundation DLCs) is, regardless of its release date, a very weird game when it comes to its mechanics, its technical features and its overall progression; too antiquated for it to be considered a "current gen" title, too ahead of its times to be considered "last gen". 

-The main story is a fascinating and intriguing journey that will make you scratch your head multiple times. There're massive payoffs in paying attention to it, but at the same time the game very clearly leaves a lot open so that it can bridge with its upcoming sequel, Control Resonant. So, despite the game having a very well written and well directed plotline, if you wanted a self-concluding experience you might end up being disappointed. 
-The lore is MASSIVE and it's actually the most interesting thing about this world, but to fully grasp it you'd need to play (at the very least) the first Alan Wake game and, in general, be familiar with the Remedyverse. It makes THAT much difference.
-On a technical standpoint, the game is a mess lol. Despite the latest update introducing DLSS4, native HDR, improvements to the RT and other graphic features... most of it is pretty much broken, even on DX12. The RT is still a boiling mess that, since the lack of Ray Reconstruction, can't be fixed without a reshade mod or disabling the native denoiser (doing so will cause other issues), so stick to rasterization. The HDR is simply awful, blurry and washed, just stick to SDR. The DLSS4, despite being a tad better than the previous version, still has extreme disocclusion issues and ghosting; it's really distracting and, regardless, pretty useless if you go full native on modern hardware. That said, even on modern hardware the game doesn't really run at super high framerates at native with max rasterized settings; It is a single player game, but it's pretty action oriented and 60fps don't feel very good (even tho the game is mostly stutter-free in my experience), b…
Really good, I 100%ed it in about 30 hours (including expansions) and I kinda wanted more. Raytracing is not worth it over medium, FPS to quality ratio wise.
